subject: POC observability plan: success criteria, dashboards, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — next steps & observability items for POC

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand how FintechX is evaluating inference for transaction classification and fraud detection. Per our call I wanted to put the proposed observability plan and success criteria in one place so we can align on owners and timeline before starting the POC.

High-level success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 token latency < 120ms for 1k concurrent requests
- Throughput: sustain 400 req/s for batch inference workload during peak window
- Cost: per-inference token cost <= $0.003 after batching/quantization
- Quality: model F1 for fraud classifier >= 0.87 on your holdout set
- Reliability: <0.5% error rate (timeouts / internal errors) over 2-week run

Observability scope (POC):
- Dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token volume, cost breakdown (tokens + infra), error rate, model version breakdown
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for 5 sample request flows (frontend -> Redwood API -> model) with root-cause tags for cache hits/misses and batching events
- Logs: request/response metadata export to your GCP logging (JSON stub: request_id, route, model_version, user_id_hash)
- Metrics to monitor: token_count, inference_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size, model_queue_length, infra_gpu_utilization

Proposed owners & timeline:
- FintechX owner: Asha (technical), Samir (procurement) — confirm
- Redwood owner: Marissa (eng sponsor/contact), Jordan (SE for tracing & instrumentation), Sean (runtime config)
- Timeline: kickoff next Wed (2027-05-05), 2-week POC window (2027-05-06 to 2027-05-20), 3-day evaluation period after run

I've attached a spreadsheet with the suggested success criteria and measurement calculations. Jordan and Sean — can you confirm the tracing and logging delivery plan below so I can share with Asha?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: POC-success-criteria.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@fintechx.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps & observability items for POC

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we lock timelines: 

1) For the latency targets: is the p95 <120ms measured from our edge to final token, or only Redwood's service time? We need the end-to-end number for SLAs.
2) GCP logging export: we will create a service account — what fields do you need exactly in the JSON payload?
3) Quality measurement: we have a 10k example holdout set — will Redwood need a private S3/GCS access or can we upload via the console?

Samir — can you confirm procurement timeline for a short-term POC commitment? We may need contract language for data residency and SOC2 evidence.

Asha
Asha Patel | Sr. Engineering Manager | FintechX
asha.patel@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps & observability items for POC

Great questions — answers below and next steps.

1) Latency: we will report both metrics. P95 (Redwood service time) and end-to-end p95 (edge -> final token). For the POC success criteria please confirm whether you want to use end-to-end p95 <120ms as the acceptance criterion or Redwood p95 <120ms (we currently recommend end-to-end).

2) GCP logging payload: minimal required fields: request_id, timestamp, route, model_version, user_id_hash, kv_cache_hit (boolean), batch_size, token_count, latency_ms, error_code (if any). We can share a JSON schema; Jordan will attach a sample.

3) Holdout upload: easiest path is to grant a short-lived GCS bucket with a service account; we can also support console upload for smaller sets. For 10k examples GCS is preferred. We'll share an upload checklist in the Drive link.

Jordan / Sean — Jordan, can you add the tracing sample and sample OpenTelemetry schema? Sean, can you confirm the KV cache export and batch metric names (so their infra team can wire them into dashboards)?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Asha to confirm acceptance criterion (end-to-end p95 or Redwood p95) by 2027-04-29
- FintechX to create GCS bucket + service account by 2027-05-03
- Redwood to provide tracing schema + dashboard templates by 2027-05-04
- Kickoff on 2027-05-05

Thanks — sharing updated SOW draft as well.

Marissa

Attachment: redwood-sow-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Tracing & logging schema for POC (sample)

Hi Asha —

Copied the key pieces below and attached a sample OpenTelemetry proto that you can forward to your infra team. Short version:
- Traces: instrument request path at these spans: frontend.receive -> api.gateway -> redwood.ingest -> model.infer -> response.serialize
- Key attributes: request_id, client_region, model_version, kv_cache_hit (true/false), batch_size, batching_delay_ms, token_count, latency_ms
- Sampling: 1% default + deterministic sampling for errors and VIP routes
- Logs: structured JSON exported to GCS via Pub/Sub; include request_id to tie logs -> traces -> metrics

Attachment: observability-dashboards.png (image/png) — includes a proposed Grafana layout (route latency, token volume, cost breakdown, batch size heatmap).

I'll drop the sample proto and OTLP snippet in the Drive folder and we can iterate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechx.com>

Thanks everyone — this plan works. To confirm:
- Acceptance: end-to-end p95 <120ms
- GCS bucket and service account created (I will share the service account email by EOD)
- Owner: Samir will own procurement/contract and I will own technical validation.
- Kickoff: 2027-05-05 at 10:00am PT — please send calendar invite

Samir — can you confirm the short-term POC budget so we can sign the SOW?

Asha
